summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Primary documents answering Q1 (ICIMOD and IPCC ranges for glacier loss and peak-water timing) were located as source leads: the ICIMOD HKH Assessment (2019, Chapter 7 on the cryosphere) and HI-WISE outlook (2023), ICIMOD Nepal glacier inventories and HKH Snow Updates (2024-2026) and Glacier Outlook 2026, IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 9, AR6 WGII Chapter 10 and Cross-Chapter Paper 5, IPCC SROCC Chapter 2, plus peer-reviewed basin and global studies (Huss and Hock 2018; Lutz et al. 2014; Rounce et al. 2023; Khadka et al. 2020 on the Koshi). No document could be downloaded (data hosts blocked), so every projection range is pending. Seven projection-range parameters are defined in specific.projection_ranges with scenario basis, metric, method and methodological cautions. Key known sources of disagreement: glacier volume vs mass vs area, differing reference years, CMIP5/RCP vs CMIP6/SSP vs warming-level framing, HKH vs RGI High Mountain Asia region definitions, and glacier-runoff vs total-runoff definitions of peak water.

findings.claim: Q1(a): ICIMOD range for HKH glacier volume loss by 2100 by warming level/pathway (HKH Assessment Ch.7, 2019; HI-WISE, 2023).
findings.note: Download leads 25A-L02 and 25A-L06; extract low/central/high per scenario; record both vintages as separate observations.

findings.claim: Q1(b): IPCC range for glacier mass change in High Mountain Asia / South Asia by 2100 by scenario (AR6 WGI Ch.9 section 9.5.1 and SM; SROCC Ch.2).
findings.note: Leads 25A-L10 to 25A-L13; use regional table for RGI South Asia East where available.

findings.claim: Q1(c): Peak-water timing for glacier runoff in the Ganges and Brahmaputra basins and in Nepal sub-basins (Koshi, Gandaki, Karnali) by scenario.
findings.period: calendar year of peak annual glacier runoff

findings.claim: Nepal basin-level projected glacier volume and area change (Koshi study located; Gandaki, Karnali, Mahakali basin studies not yet located).
findings.note: Lead 25A-L23 for Koshi; r2 must locate Gandaki/Karnali/Mahakali studies.

findings.claim: Observed snow-persistence anomalies for winters 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26 across HKH basins, including the Ganges basin.
Dry-season melt contribution to flow at Nepal hydropower catchments (parameter for Agent 05 and 22D).

Projection ranges are carried as scenario-conditional ranges (low/central/high per emission pathway or warming level), never collapsed into a single probability-weighted value; scenarios are stress tests, not forecasts.

Where ICIMOD and IPCC ranges differ, both are retained with model ensemble, reference period, region definition and variable (mass, volume, area) recorded; no source is silently preferred despite ICIMOD and IPCC sharing catalog tier 6.

data_gaps: No download of any lead was possible in r1; all projection ranges pending.
Basin-scale projections for Gandaki, Karnali and Mahakali (Nepal side) not yet located; only a Koshi study was found.
Hydropower-catchment-level dry-season flow projections (project-scale) not located; needed by Agent 05/22D.
DHM (tier 1) observed discharge series for glacier-fed rivers not located as downloadable files.
Whether HI-WISE (2023) provides basin-specific peak-water years for Nepal sub-basins must be checked on retrieval.
Web search budget was exhausted during r1; further leads (e.g. DHM hydrological yearbooks, WECS basin plans) must be located in r2.

assumptions.text: The HKH region follows ICIMOD's definition; IPCC and global studies use RGI regions (South Asia East covers the Nepal Himalaya). Values are mapped only where the source reports the matching region; otherwise the aggregate is labelled with its own region.

Projected climate parameters are on calendar-year or multi-decade horizons; conversion to Nepal FY is not meaningful for these ranges and they enter the model only as scenario parameters for S05 and S09.
Peak water refers to annual glacier runoff unless the source states otherwise; total river-flow change is carried as a separate parameter (PR-05).

challenges.text: Hydropower generation paths should not assume stationary dry-season flow; request that Agent 05 take PR-05/PR-07 ranges (when retrieved) as scenario parameters and report sensitivity rather than a point path.
X17 (hydrology and cryosphere change) is a range-valued, scenario-conditional input, not a time series; the deliverable description in global_task_list should allow scenario-conditional ranges.
Source catalog has no id for DHM hydrological yearbooks beyond 'dhm' generic entry, nor for peer-reviewed glacier studies other than the generic 'academic'; suggest specific ids for traceability.

uncertainty: High. Structural uncertainty spans emission pathway, GCM precipitation spread, glacier-model physics (debris cover, dynamics) and reference-period choice. Peak-water timing is especially sensitive to definition (annual vs monthly; glacier vs total runoff). All values pending; no ranges are yet recorded as observations.

projection_ranges.method: Extract low/central/high per scenario from HKH Assessment Ch.7 tables and HI-WISE 2023; keep both vintages separately
projection_ranges.methodological_notes: HKH Assessment (2019, CMIP5/RCP) vs HI-WISE (2023, warming levels, newer glacier models): different model ensembles and baselines; keep both and report the difference

projection_ranges.variable: High Mountain Asia / South Asia glacier mass change to 2100
projection_ranges.spatial_scope: RGI regions for South Asia East, South Asia West, Central Asia
projection_ranges.scenario_basis: SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5 (AR6 WGI); RCP2.6/RCP8.5 (SROCC); warming levels (Rounce 2023)

projection_ranges.method: Extract regional values for RGI South Asia East (Nepal Himalaya) where tabulated; otherwise HMA aggregate labelled as such
projection_ranges.methodological_notes: IPCC chapters assess published model ensembles; Rounce et al. is a single-model-framework study relative to 2015; mass vs volume vs area are not interchangeable

projection_ranges.spatial_scope: Koshi basin (Nepal + TAR); Karnali, Gandaki, Mahakali where available
projection_ranges.metric: percent of source-baseline glacier volume and area
projection_ranges.scenario_basis: RCP4.5 / RCP8.5 (Khadka 2020); SSP scenarios in newer basin studies
projection_ranges.baseline_period: pending (extract from source; differs by source)
projection_ranges.method: Basin-level ranges per study; attach model (OGGM+GDM etc.) and baseline; Karnali/Gandaki studies still to be located in r2
projection_ranges.methodological_notes: Area loss and volume loss diverge; debris-covered glaciers respond differently; basin boundaries cross into TAR

projection_ranges.variable: Peak water timing (annual glacier melt runoff)
projection_ranges.spatial_scope: Ganges, Brahmaputra (and Nepal sub-basins Koshi, Gandaki, Karnali)
projection_ranges.metric: calendar year (or decade) of peak annual glacier runoff
projection_ranges.scenario_basis: RCP/SSP or warming level per source
projection_ranges.unit: calendar year (or decade) of peak annual glacier runoff
projection_ranges.baseline_period: pending (extract from source; differs by source)
projection_ranges.method: Extract peak-water year/decade by basin and scenario from Huss and Hock (2018), HI-WISE, SROCC Ch.2, Rounce (2023) and basin studies; record 'already passed' where stated
projection_ranges.methodological_notes: Peak water defined for glacier runoff only (not total river flow) in most sources; timing is later for more glacierised basins and higher emission scenarios; monthly peak differs from annual peak

projection_ranges.variable: Total river runoff change to mid-century
projection_ranges.spatial_scope: Upper Ganges and Brahmaputra; Nepal sub-basins
projection_ranges.metric: percent change in mean annual and seasonal runoff vs reference period
projection_ranges.scenario_basis: RCP4.5 / RCP8.5 (Lutz 2014); SSPs in AR6-era studies
projection_ranges.baseline_period: pending (extract from source; differs by source)
projection_ranges.method: Separate annual vs dry-season (Dec-May) changes; dry-season change is the hydropower-relevant parameter for Agent 05
projection_ranges.methodological_notes: Precipitation-driven increases can mask melt decline; GCM precipitation spread is the dominant uncertainty

projection_ranges.spatial_scope: HKH basins incl. Ganges; Nepal sub-basins where reported
projection_ranges.metric: percent anomaly vs MODIS-era baseline (observed) and percent change in snow cover (projected)
projection_ranges.scenario_basis: Observed anomalies (Snow Updates 2024-2026); projected change in HI-WISE
projection_ranges.baseline_period: pending (extract from source; differs by source)
projection_ranges.method: Observed annual anomalies are facts once retrieved; projected ranges are estimates; do not mix
projection_ranges.methodological_notes: Snow persistence (ICIMOD MODIS index) is not snow water equivalent; baselines are short (post-2003)

projection_ranges.variable: Melt contribution to dry-season flow at hydropower sites
projection_ranges.spatial_scope: Nepal run-of-river project catchments by basin
projection_ranges.metric: percent of dry-season flow from snow and glacier melt
projection_ranges.baseline_period: pending (extract from source; differs by source)
projection_ranges.method: Supply as parameter for Agent 05 (hydro generation) and 22D; attach catchment and season definition
projection_ranges.methodological_notes: Contribution varies strongly with catchment elevation; national averages are misleading for project-level generation
